items.item_text: BART or BLS at time of hire with commitment to get BART within six (6) months of hire date.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
One (1+) or more years of relevant experience.

The Physical Therapist Assistant will work in a dynamic outpatient setting and provide treatments to a wide variety of orthopedic patients. The employee will implement therapeutic exercises, modalities, and manual techniques under the supervision of a physical therapist. Treatment provided will follow therapy procedures, protocols and programs. Patient progress will be documented and communicated effectively with the primary therapist. Employee will work under general supervision and also assist with inventory control, clinic maintenance and organization. Should also be able to excel in working within a collaborative environment and communicate patient information across the continuum of care.
Depending on the experience of the selected candidate, this position will be hired at the Physical Therapist Assistant I, II or III level.
Physical Therapy Assistant (PTA) issued by the state of California.

Be a self-starter who is accountable and requires minimal direction and supervision; a person who is open to new ideas; and a creative and flexible individual who is comfortable working in a large, complex organization.
Possesses the ability to treat patients, follow an established plan of care and performvarious physical therapy treatments appropriate to acute care.
Ability to determine expected outcomes throughout the continuum of therapeutic intervention.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to communicate clearly both verbally and in writing and be able to articulate complex ideas for all levels of audiences.
Possess the personal characteristics of professionalism, credibility, commitment to high standards, innovation, discriminating judgment, and accountability.
